candidate.frozen_unchanged: internal/core, internal/py, conformance/cases (git diff cbfe3d9..669648c empty for these); main and installed preview untouched

changed_behaviour.never_acked_escalation: Tick -> unacked(): timed-out + no ack for 60 s -> duty (principal checked); director at 120 s or at once if duty unreachable; failed send recorded 'failed <t>: <why>' and retried each pass, never 'sent'; not an ack or a recovery.
changed_behaviour.achievable_bound: duty: <= 60 s + pass interval (--every, 30 s) + pass time after settlement (about 90-95 s); director: <= 120 s + 30 s + pass time; NO escalation while run is stopped (liveness check owns that); L6 still needs a real ack <= 60 s after detection.
changed_behaviour.early_callback: no-op-early -> RearmEarly: only the running step's current action (phase RUNNING, duty principal bound); same unit, original ledger instant (never now+duration); spent unit stopped+reset; replay while waiting reuses it (one due timer); failed re-arm and every re-arm told to duty; nothing cancelled, dispatched or settled.
changed_behaviour.duplicate_notice: only: failed-cancel settlement notice + the later replay's core wake, same T-<action> incident; no per-pass flood, no second cancel/dispatch; any other duplicate is a defect

host_effects: transient p12test-stop-closure-* units (3) created and removed; no daemon-reload in this closure; no seats, main, install or clock change
residuals: Injected-clock (core.FakeClock) tests prove the loop side only; systemd's calendar delivery after a real host clock rollback is NOT established. Qualification assumes continuous host UTC; a real discontinuity invalidates the timing sample and needs reconciliation.

A re-arm happens only if the early callback runs; if systemd never fires the unit (e.g. a large backward step before firing), nothing in the loop sees it until the liveness check; that is not changed here.
No escalation of an unacked timeout while run is stopped.
A re-armed unit is not in the stop path of disarm (same unit name, so disarm's stop of <unit>.timer does cover it) -- covered because the name is unchanged.
L4a/L4b, live ack latency and step-timer precision on real seats: proved only in the signed live run.
